questions.stem:
Statement: 'Students who study regularly perform better in examinations.'
Assumptions: I. Regular study is the only factor that determines exam performance. II. There is a positive correlation between regular study and exam results.
Which assumption(s) is/are implicit?
questions.explanation: Assumption I says regular study is the ONLY factor — this is too extreme. The statement says students who study regularly perform BETTER, not that it's the sole factor. Assumption II (positive correlation between regular study and performance) is exactly what the statement implies — it is implicit. Only II is implicit.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statement: 'The government has decided to provide free mid-day meals to all school children.'
Assumptions: I. School children need nutritional support to perform well. II. All school children are malnourished.
Which assumption(s) is/are implicit?
questions.explanation: Assumption I (children need nutritional support to perform well) is implicit — the action of providing meals presupposes nutrition helps children. Assumption II (all children are malnourished) is NOT implicit; the policy could target any child for equity reasons, not necessarily because all are malnourished. Only I is implicit.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statement: 'Do not lean out of the window while the train is moving.' (sign inside a train)
Assumptions: I. Leaning out while the train moves can be dangerous. II. Passengers sometimes tend to lean out of windows.
Which assumption(s) is/are implicit?
questions.explanation: A warning sign is put only when there is a real danger (Assumption I is implicit) AND when people actually do the unsafe thing (Assumption II is implicit — there's no point warning against something nobody does). Both I and II are implicit.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statement: 'Eat fresh fruits daily to stay healthy.'
Assumptions: I. Fresh fruits contain nutrients necessary for health. II. People who eat fresh fruits never fall ill.
Which assumption(s) is/are implicit?
questions.explanation: Assumption I is implicit — advising people to eat fruits to stay healthy presupposes that fruits contribute to health. Assumption II ('never fall ill') is an absolute claim the statement does not make — the statement only says 'to stay healthy', not 'to avoid all illness'. Only I is implicit.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statement: 'Please switch off the lights when you leave the room.' (notice in office)
Assumptions: I. People sometimes leave the lights on when they leave. II. Electricity is expensive and should not be wasted.
Which assumption(s) is/are implicit?
questions.explanation: A notice is issued to correct existing behaviour — so Assumption I (people do leave lights on) is implicit. The instruction also assumes that leaving lights on wastes resources, making Assumption II (electricity should not be wasted) implicit. Both I and II are implicit.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statement: 'The company has decided to advertise its product on social media platforms.'
Assumptions: I. Social media platforms are effective in reaching potential customers. II. The company's product is popular on social media already.
Which assumption(s) is/are implicit?
questions.explanation: Choosing social media for advertising implies the company believes it is an effective channel — Assumption I is implicit. Assumption II (already popular on social media) cannot be assumed just because the company is choosing to advertise there; the purpose of advertising is often to build that popularity, not presuppose it. Only I is implicit.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statement: 'Parents should encourage children to solve puzzles to improve their logical thinking.'
Assumptions: I. Children can improve their logical thinking through practice. II. Solving puzzles is the only way to improve logical thinking in children.
Which assumption(s) is/are implicit?
questions.explanation: The statement assumes logical thinking can be improved through activities like puzzle-solving, so Assumption I is implicit. Assumption II says puzzles are the ONLY way — this is too strong; the statement recommends puzzles without ruling out other methods. Only I is implicit.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statement: 'Travelling by air is faster than travelling by train for long distances.'
Assumptions: I. Air travel is always available for all long-distance routes. II. Speed is an important factor when people choose their mode of travel.
Which assumption(s) is/are implicit?
questions.explanation: Assumption I (air travel is always available everywhere) is NOT implicit — the statement is a general comparison of speed, not a claim about universal availability. Assumption II (speed matters to travellers) is implicit because the statement compares modes by speed, which only makes sense if the audience values speed when choosing travel mode. Only II is implicit.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statement: 'If you want to lose weight, reduce your sugar intake.'
Assumptions: I. Sugar intake is one of the causes of weight gain. II. Reducing sugar alone is sufficient to lose weight.
Which assumption(s) is/are implicit?
questions.explanation: The advice to reduce sugar to lose weight assumes sugar contributes to weight gain (Assumption I is implicit). Assumption II says reducing sugar is SUFFICIENT — the statement says 'reduce sugar to lose weight', which implies it helps, not that it is the only action needed. Assumption II is too strong. Only I is implicit.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statement: 'The bank manager said: We offer home loans at the lowest interest rate in the market.'
Assumptions: I. Customers consider interest rates when choosing a bank for home loans. II. All other banks offer home loans at higher interest rates.
Which assumption(s) is/are implicit?
questions.explanation: The bank highlights low interest to attract customers — this assumes customers are influenced by interest rates when choosing (Assumption I is implicit). Claiming 'lowest in the market' also assumes that other banks charge more (Assumption II is implicit, as 'lowest' is a comparative superlative). Both I and II are implicit.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statement: 'A city planner recommended building more parks to reduce traffic congestion.'
Assumptions: I. Parks can divert people away from roads and reduce vehicle usage. II. Lack of parks is the only cause of traffic congestion.
Which assumption(s) is/are implicit?
questions.explanation: The recommendation assumes parks help reduce congestion somehow — perhaps by providing local leisure destinations and reducing car trips — so Assumption I is implicit. Assumption II claims parks are the ONLY cause, which is far too narrow; traffic congestion has many causes. Only I is implicit.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statement: 'The school has introduced a new teaching method to improve students' comprehension.'
Assumptions: I. The current teaching method is not fully effective. II. The new teaching method will definitely improve comprehension for all students.
Which assumption(s) is/are implicit?
questions.explanation: Introducing a new method to improve comprehension implies the existing method has room for improvement (Assumption I is implicit — otherwise, why change?). Assumption II says it will 'definitely' improve comprehension for ALL students — this is too absolute. The school aims to improve, not guarantees universal success. Only I is implicit.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statement: 'The doctor advised Meena to avoid cold drinks to get relief from her throat infection.'
Assumptions: I. Cold drinks can worsen throat infections. II. Meena is willing to follow the doctor's advice.
Which assumption(s) is/are implicit?
questions.explanation: Advising someone to avoid cold drinks for throat relief assumes cold drinks aggravate the condition (Assumption I is implicit). Giving advice also presupposes the patient will follow it — there is no point advising an unwilling patient (Assumption II is implicit). Both I and II are implicit.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statement: 'A software company decided to hire more engineers to complete the project on time.'
Assumptions: I. Adding more engineers will speed up the project completion. II. The current team lacks the capacity to complete the project on time.
Which assumption(s) is/are implicit?
questions.explanation: Hiring more engineers to meet a deadline assumes more manpower will accelerate work (Assumption I is implicit) AND that the current team cannot finish in time (Assumption II is implicit — if they could, additional hiring would be unnecessary). Both I and II are implicit.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statement: 'An NGO launched a campaign urging people to use public transport instead of private vehicles to reduce pollution.'
Assumptions: I. Private vehicles contribute significantly to air pollution. II. A majority of people currently use public transport.
Which assumption(s) is/are implicit?
questions.explanation: The campaign to switch from private to public transport to reduce pollution assumes that private vehicles are a significant pollution source (Assumption I is implicit). Assumption II (most people already use public transport) is actually the OPPOSITE of what the campaign presupposes — the campaign urges switching, implying many currently use private vehicles. Assumption II is not implicit. Only I is implicit.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statement: 'To improve discipline, the school has made attendance of morning assembly mandatory for all students.'
Assumptions: I. Morning assembly helps in building discipline. II. Students who miss morning assembly have poor discipline.
Which assumption(s) is/are implicit?
questions.explanation: Making assembly mandatory to improve discipline assumes that assembly contributes to building discipline (Assumption I is implicit). Assumption II says students who miss assembly have poor discipline — this is a consequence claim, not a presupposition of the action. The school is not targeting poorly disciplined students; it is a universal measure. Assumption II is not implicit. Only I is implicit.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statement: 'Despite warnings, a number of pilgrims attempted to climb the snow-covered peak.'
Assumptions: I. The pilgrims were aware of the warnings. II. Climbing snow-covered peaks is always life-threatening.
Which assumption(s) is/are implicit?
questions.explanation: The word 'despite' explicitly means they knew about the warnings but proceeded anyway — Assumption I (awareness of warnings) is implicit in the use of 'despite'. Assumption II (always life-threatening) is too absolute; the statement mentions warnings of danger in a specific context, not a universal law. Only I is implicit.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statement: 'You should read the label carefully before taking any medicine.'
Assumptions: I. Medicine labels contain important dosage and safety information. II. People generally do not read medicine labels carefully.
Which assumption(s) is/are implicit?
questions.explanation: Asking someone to read a label 'carefully' implies the label has useful, important information (Assumption I is implicit). The use of 'should' (an advisory) also implies that this is a behaviour people currently neglect — otherwise the advice is unnecessary (Assumption II is implicit). Both I and II are implicit.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statement: 'A teacher told a slow learner: You can definitely pass if you revise each chapter twice.'
Assumptions: I. The student has the ability to understand and revise the chapters. II. Revising each chapter twice guarantees passing for every student.
Which assumption(s) is/are implicit?
questions.explanation: The advice is directed at this specific student — the teacher would not give such advice if she believed the student incapable. Assumption I (the student can revise and understand) is implicit. Assumption II says it 'guarantees passing for every student' — the statement is a personal encouragement to one student, not a universal law. Assumption II is not implicit. Only I is implicit.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statement: 'The municipal corporation has banned use of plastic bags in the city to keep the environment clean.'
Assumptions: I. Plastic bags cause environmental pollution. II. People will obey the ban and stop using plastic bags.
Which assumption(s) is/are implicit?
questions.explanation: Banning plastic bags to clean the environment assumes plastic bags pollute it (Assumption I is implicit). Enacting a ban also assumes it will be followed — a law that is assumed to be universally ignored would be pointless to enact (Assumption II is implicit). Both I and II are implicit.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statement: 'The management has asked employees to submit their weekly reports by Friday evening, not Monday morning as was the practice.'
Assumptions: I. Employees were previously submitting reports on Monday mornings. II. Friday submission will allow management to review reports over the weekend.
Which assumption(s) is/are implicit?
questions.explanation: The statement explicitly says '...not Monday morning as was the practice', confirming Monday was the old practice — Assumption I is implicit (and actually stated). The change to Friday suggests a purpose: enabling review over the weekend, making Assumption II implicit. Both I and II are implicit.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statement: 'The airline claims it guarantees on-time departure for 95% of its flights.'
Assumptions: I. On-time departure is a factor that passengers consider when choosing an airline. II. The remaining 5% of flights will be delayed by at least an hour.
Which assumption(s) is/are implicit?
questions.explanation: The airline advertises its on-time record to attract passengers, so it assumes passengers value punctuality (Assumption I is implicit). Assumption II specifies the delay duration for the remaining 5% as 'at least an hour' — the statement says nothing about the extent of delays, only that 5% are not on time. This detail is not assumed. Only I is implicit.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statement: 'Ramesh was advised to join a coaching class to crack the competitive exam.'
Assumptions: I. Coaching classes can help candidates improve their exam performance. II. Ramesh cannot crack the exam without joining a coaching class.
Which assumption(s) is/are implicit?
questions.explanation: Recommending coaching assumes it provides an advantage (Assumption I is implicit). Assumption II says coaching is the ONLY way for Ramesh — this is too strong; the advisor recommends coaching as helpful, not as the exclusive path. Many candidates crack competitive exams through self-study. Only I is implicit.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statement: 'The government has decided to increase the number of ITI (Industrial Training Institutes) in rural areas.'
Assumptions: I. Rural areas currently have fewer ITIs than urban areas. II. Skilled workers produced by ITIs can find employment and improve rural livelihoods.
Which assumption(s) is/are implicit?
questions.explanation: Increasing ITIs in rural areas specifically implies current rural coverage is insufficient (Assumption I is implicit). The government would invest in ITIs only if it believes they produce employable skilled workers who can improve livelihoods (Assumption II is implicit — this is the underlying rationale). Both I and II are implicit.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statement: 'Higher the number of choices, higher will be the voter turnout in elections.'
Assumptions: I. Voters are motivated by the quality or variety of candidates available. II. Elections with only two candidates always have lower turnout than those with three or more.
Which assumption(s) is/are implicit?
questions.explanation: The statement assumes that having more candidates to choose from motivates more voters to participate — so Assumption I (voters respond to candidate variety) is implicit. Assumption II is a specific quantitative claim (2 candidates vs 3+) that goes beyond what the statement asserts. The statement says 'higher the choices → higher turnout' as a general tendency, not a strict threshold comparison. Only I is implicit.
